confirmed.title: focus_before_lock_ handle can match a recycled heap address and focus the wrong window on unlock (no freed read)
confirmed.scenario: User focuses window A; session locks (handleSessionLocked:1764 stashes focus_before_lock_ = A). While locked, client destroys A (toplevel destroy -> removeView frees the View; focus_before_lock_ is intentionally left stale — it is a handle, never scrubbed). Still locked, another client creates a toplevel (new_xdg_toplevel at Server.cc:173 is not lock-gated), and the allocator reuses A's freed address for the new View — plausible since Views are uniform-size heap objects freed and allocated in close succession. On unlock, handleSessionUnlocked:1772 calls viewForHandle(focus_before_lock_), which pointer-compares and now MATCHES the impostor, so focus lands on a window the user never had focused (potentially off-workspace, since the restore path does not check workspace the way setCurrentWorkspace's restore branch does). No dereference of freed memory ever occurs — viewForHandle only compares — so this is a correctness/UX bug, not a UAF; reported because it is the one place in the input/focus state where a dangling value survives by design and the re-validation is by address equality rather than a generation-checked id.
confirmed.event_sequence:
Preconditions: one headless output booted. Actor list: user (input), client-A (the pre-lock app), a locker client (ext-session-lock-v1), client-B (the impostor app). All events are protocol-legal.

1. client-A: wl_compositor.create_surface; xdg_wm_base.get_xdg_surface; xdg_surface.get_toplevel  -> server new_toplevel fires -> Server.cc:173 pushes View A into `views` at heap address X. client-A commits a buffer -> View A maps.
2. user: pointer-click / focus lands on View A -> Server.focused_view = A.
3. locker: ext_session_lock_manager_v1.lock. Server drives SessionLock; fallback path or lock-surface commit sets locked_ = true, then calls Server::handleSessionLocked(takeover=false) -> Server.cc:1764 stashes focus_before_lock_ = A (== X). clearFocus() nulls focused_view.
4. client-A (still connected, lock does NOT gate xdg teardown): destroy xdg_toplevel (or disconnect). View::toplevel_destroy_ (View.cc:77-78) fires -> Server::removeView(A) (Server.cc:623) runs unconditionally, `views.erase(it)` frees the View at address X. removeView scrubs six cached pointers but NOT focus_before_lock_, so it still holds X (dangling by design, Server.hh:483).
5. client-B (new client, or client-A again — new_toplevel is NOT lock-gated): wl_compositor.create_surface; get_xdg_surface; get_toplevel -> Server.cc:173 `views.push_back(std::make_unique<View>(...))`. Because View is a fixed-size heap object and X was the most-recently-freed block of that size, glibc tcache LIFO reuse hands the new View the same address X (probabilistic, but the single free-then-alloc of a same-size object is the textbook reuse case). client-B does NOT commit a buffer -> View B exists in `views`, base->initialized == false, isMapped() == false.
6. locker: ext_session_lock_v1.unlock_and_destroy (or crash). SessionLock::onUnlock (SessionLock.cc:128-131) sets locked_ = false BEFORE calling Server::handleSessionUnlocked (Server.cc:1769). There viewForHandle(focus_before_lock_) (Server.cc:1783) pointer-compares X against every live View and MATCHES impostor B — an ABA hit, undetectable because the check is address equality with no generation id and no isMapped() guard (unlike topmostViewOnWorkspace). focusView(B) (Server.cc:887) proceeds (lock gate already dropped) and calls wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated + wlr_seat_keyboard_notify_enter on an unmapped, uninitialized toplevel. Divergence is observable because the correct fallback (Server.cc:1773) would have skipped B (not mapped) and cleared focus; instead focus lands on a window the user never had focused.

No read of freed memory ever occurs (viewForHandle only compares addresses). The set_activated/keyboard_notify_enter on an uninitialized toplevel is a POSSIBLE abort in wlroots 0.20 (could not confirm an initialized-assert — wlroots sources are not on this machine), but the confirmed, certain outcome is wrong-window focus.

confirmed.title: Focused client unmapping (NULL-buffer commit, role kept) is never tracked: the next focus transition calls wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated on a reset xdg surface -> assert(surface->initialized) -> SIGABRT
confirmed.scenario: Client A holds focus. A hides its window the xdg way: wl_surface.attach(NULL)+commit (GTK gtk_widget_hide, app closing a reusable window) - wlroots 0.20.1 xdg_surface_role_commit runs reset_xdg_surface (initialized=false) but does NOT emit toplevel destroy, so View A and Server::focused_view survive (View::unmap_ only flips mapped). User then clicks window B, or sloppy-focus moves the pointer over B, or switches workspace, or iconifies B - any path into focusView(B) or clearFocus() first calls wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated(focused_view->toplevel(), false) [Server.cc:898, clearFocus at :1728] -> wlr_xdg_surface_schedule_configure -> assert(surface->initialized) fails (wlroots types/xdg_shell/wlr_xdg_surface.c:168; gotcha #13 confirms this assert fires on the installed Fedora build) -> compositor aborts, live session dies. Root fix surface: an onViewUnmapped hook that parks focus (mirroring removeView's handoff), plus mapped-gates before every wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_* below.
confirmed.event_sequence:
Two-client path (primary, no pointer needed; focusNewWindows=true and focusModel=SloppyFocus are defaults):

1. Client A: wl_compositor.create_surface -> xdg_wm_base.get_xdg_surface -> xdg_surface.get_toplevel -> (optional set_mode SSD) -> wl_surface.commit (no buffer) -> receives xdg_surface.configure -> ack_configure -> wl_surface.attach(bufA) -> commit. Compositor maps A: View::map_ -> onViewMapped -> focusView(A) -> focused_view = A.
2. Client A hides the window the xdg way (GTK gtk_widget_hide / app closing a reusable window): wl_surface.attach(NULL, 0, 0) then wl_surface.commit. Compositor: surface_commit_state (wlr_compositor.c:517) sees invalid_buffer && buffer==NULL -> unmap_commit=true -> wlr_surface_unmap; xdg_surface_role_commit (wlr_xdg_surface.c:319) -> reset_xdg_surface_role_object + reset_xdg_surface sets initialized=false, does NOT emit toplevel destroy. View A survives (lifetime bound to toplevel destroy), View::unmap_ sets mapped=false only; focused_view still == A.
3. Client B: create_surface / get_xdg_surface / get_toplevel / commit / ack / attach(bufB) / commit. Compositor maps B: onViewMapped -> config_.focusNewWindows -> focusView(B). Inside focusView (Server.cc:896) focused_view(A) != B, so line 898 runs wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated(A->toplevel(), false) on A's reset surface -> wlr_xdg_surface_schedule_configure -> assert(surface->initialized) FAILS -> SIGABRT.

Single-client variant (same steps 1-2, then a user gesture instead of client B):
3'. User presses Super+Right (or an ext-workspace pager activate) to switch to an empty workspace. Server::setCurrentWorkspace(i) (Server.cc:1865): incoming ws has no remembered/topmost view -> clearFocus() (line 1885) -> line 1728 wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated(focused_view(A)->toplevel(), false) -> assert(initialized) -> SIGABRT.

Both A's steps are protocol-legal (NULL-buffer commit that keeps the xdg role is the standard hide gesture); the user gesture in the single-client variant is a plain workspace switch.

confirmed.title: Snap/ToggleFullscreen/CloseWindow-adjacent bindings operate on the stale unmapped focused_view: set_size/set_fullscreen/set_tiled assert the same way
confirmed.scenario: Same setup: focused client A unmaps (role alive), focused_view still points at A and no input happened yet to change focus. User presses the SnapLeft/SnapRight binding -> snapFocused derefs focused_view, calls v->resizeTo (View.cc:182 wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_size) and wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_tiled (Server.cc:1494) -> schedule_configure asserts initialized -> abort. Identical trigger via the ToggleFullscreen binding (executeAction:1709 -> setViewFullscreen -> View::setFullscreen View.cc:160 wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_fullscreen). Same root as finding 1.
confirmed.event_sequence:
1. Client A connects, creates wl_surface -> xdg_surface -> xdg_toplevel, does the initial (bufferless) commit, receives xdg_surface.configure, acks, attaches an SHM buffer and commits. wlroots maps the surface; Server::onViewMapped runs and, with the default session.focusNewWindows=true (Config.hh:72, Server.cc:686), focusView(A) sets Server::focused_view = A's View.
2. Client A hides its window the protocol-legal way: wl_surface_attach(surface, NULL, 0, 0); wl_surface_commit(). (Real-world: a tray app hiding to tray, a splash screen, a client withdrawing during reconfigure.) In wlroots this is an unmap_commit: xdg_surface_role_commit (types/xdg_shell/wlr_xdg_surface.c:319-324) calls reset_xdg_surface, which sets surface->initialized = false (line 28) while the wlr_xdg_toplevel role object stays alive (only its state is reset). View's unmap listener (src/View.cc:51-54) sets mapped=false and clears the decoration; it does NOT tell the Server, so focused_view still points at A (scrubbed only in removeView, Server.cc:641-642).
3. With no intervening input that changes focus, the user presses Super+Shift+Left (default SnapLeft binding, Keybindings.cc:29). onKey -> dispatchBinding (Server.cc:1684) -> executeAction case SnapLeft (1712) -> snapFocused(WLR_EDGE_LEFT) (1474): focused_view non-null, outputForView is purely geometric (751-757, falls back to active_output) so non-null, no isMapped() guard -> v->resizeTo (1491) -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_size (View.cc:182) -> wlr_xdg_surface_schedule_configure -> assert(surface->initialized) (wlr_xdg_surface.c:168, compiled into the shipped Fedora lib) -> SIGABRT, killing the live session.
Equivalent step 3 variants: Super+f (ToggleFullscreen, Server.cc:1709 -> setViewFullscreen -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_fullscreen, View.cc:160 - setFullscreen(v, !isFullscreen()) always flips so the fullscreen_==on early-return at View.cc:152 never saves it), and Super+Ctrl+Arrow (MoveToOutput -> moveFocusedToOutput, Server.cc:1497, on a multi-head layout). CloseWindow (Super+q) is NOT affected: wlr_xdg_toplevel_send_close does no schedule_configure.

confirmed.title: cancelCycle restores focus to cycle_start_ without an isMapped check - Escape after the session-start window unmapped mid-cycle aborts
confirmed.scenario: Focus on A; user opens alt-tab (cycle_start_=A) and Tabs to a preview of B. While the modifier is held, client A unmaps (NULL-buffer commit; removeView never runs so cycle_start_ is not nulled - only destroy prunes it). User presses Escape -> cancelCycle -> focusView(start): start!=focused_view so no early-out, deactivates B (fine, mapped), then wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated(A, true) at Server.cc:902 on the reset surface -> assert -> abort. commitCycle:978 has the exact isMapped guard this path lacks.
confirmed.event_sequence:
1. Client A connects: bind wl_compositor/xdg_wm_base/wl_shm; create wl_surface -> xdg_surface -> xdg_toplevel; initial (bufferless) commit; on configure: ack_configure, attach an shm wl_buffer, commit. View A maps.
2. Client B does the same. View B maps. Both windows on the current workspace.
3. User clicks A's titlebar -> focusView(A): focused_view = A, MRU front = A. (Order: create B first, then A, so A is topmost; or click A's frame directly.)
4. User presses and HOLDS Alt, taps Tab -> keybinding Action::CycleNext -> cycleStep(+1): cycling_=true, cycle_ring_ frozen [A,B], cycle_start_ = A, preview raises+focuses B (focused_view = B, MRU untouched).
5. While Alt is still held, client A unmaps WITHOUT destroying anything: wl_surface_attach(surface, NULL, 0, 0); wl_surface_commit(surface). Protocol-legal per xdg-shell ("attaching a null buffer unmaps the surface"). In wlroots 0.20.1 this fires surface unmap (View A's unmap_ listener sets mapped=false, View.cc:51-54 -- Server never notified, cycle_start_ NOT cleared) and reset_xdg_surface sets base->initialized=false while the xdg_toplevel role object stays alive (no destroy event, so removeView never runs).
6. User presses Escape (Alt still held) -> onKey Escape-while-cycling funnel (Server.cc:1633) -> cancelCycle() (Server.cc:1000): start = A (non-null, unmapped). focusView(A): A != focused_view(B) so no early-out at line 896; line 898 deactivates B (mapped, harmless); line 902 wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated(A->toplevel(), true) -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_schedule_configure -> wlr_xdg_surface_schedule_configure -> assert(surface->initialized) at wlr_xdg_surface.c:168 -> abort(). Compositor (and the live session) dies.

confirmed.title: deiconifyView focuses an icon whose client unmapped while iconified (icon menu / Deiconify action) - same assert
confirmed.scenario: User iconifies window A (titlebar button); A's client later unmaps the surface while hidden (role kept; nothing prunes icons_ - only destroy does). User middle-clicks the desktop, opens the icon menu (A still listed - buildIconMenu has no mapped filter), clicks A's row -> activateMenuItem Act::Deiconify -> viewForHandle succeeds -> deiconifyView: raiseView (safe) then focusView(v) -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated on the reset surface -> assert -> abort.
confirmed.event_sequence:
1. Client A connects, creates wl_surface -> xdg_surface -> xdg_toplevel (+ SSD decoration), commits, acks configure, attaches an shm buffer, commits -> mapped View A. Client B does the same (B exists only so the desktop stays deterministic; the bug also reproduces with A alone, since iconifyView then hits clearFocus()).
2. USER: moves pointer onto A's titlebar iconify button, left press + release -> dispatchButtonRelease(Part::IconifyButton) -> iconifyView(A) (src/Server.cc:1394): A->setIconified(true), icons_.push_back(A), focus moves to B (topmostViewOnWorkspace filters isIconified) or is cleared. focused_view != A from here on.
3. CLIENT A (protocol-legal withdraw, exactly what GTK does on gtk_widget_hide): wl_surface.attach(NULL, 0, 0); wl_surface.commit. In wlroots 0.20.1 this is an unmap_commit: wlr_surface unmap event fires (View unmap listener src/View.cc:51-54 sets mapped=false, nothing more), then xdg_surface_role_commit -> reset_xdg_surface_role_object + reset_xdg_surface (types/xdg_shell/wlr_xdg_surface.c:319-321) -> surface->initialized=false, configured=false. The wlr_xdg_toplevel OBJECT survives (only reset, not freed), so View::toplevel() stays a valid pointer to a reset toplevel. icons_ still contains A: the only erase site is removeView (src/Server.cc:637), reached only from toplevel destroy (src/View.cc:77).
4. USER: middle-clicks bare desktop -> openIconMenu (src/Server.cc:2159) -> buildIconMenu (src/Server.cc:2146) iterates icons_ with NO mapped filter; A's row appears (reset/NULL title absorbed by the "(unnamed)" fallback at :2151).
5. USER: left-presses A's row -> handleMenuButton (src/Server.cc:2274, activates on press) -> activateMenuItem{Act::Deiconify, target=A->windowID()} (src/Server.cc:2251) -> viewForHandle (src/Server.cc:1783, identity search, no mapped filter) returns A -> deiconifyView(A) (src/Server.cc:2177): setIconified(false)/setWorkspace/raiseView are scene-only and survive; then focusView(A) at src/Server.cc:2187. focusView (src/Server.cc:902): focused_view != A so no early return -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_activated(A->toplevel(), true) -> wlr_xdg_surface_schedule_configure -> assert(surface->initialized) at wlroots types/xdg_shell/wlr_xdg_surface.c:168 -> SIGABRT. The dogfooded session dies.

confirmed.title: Window-menu MaximizeToggle on a target that unmapped while the menu was open calls wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_maximized on a reset surface
confirmed.scenario: User right-clicks A's titlebar -> window menu opens (input is modal, but the wayland event loop still dispatches client requests). Client A unmaps via NULL-buffer commit while the menu is up. User clicks 'Maximize' -> activateMenuItem Act::MaximizeToggle -> viewForHandle(copy.target) still finds A (alive, just unmapped) -> v->setMaximized -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_maximized (View.cc:129) -> schedule_configure asserts initialized -> abort. Act::Close on the same menu is safe (send_close is a plain event, no configure - verified in wlroots source), which shows the asymmetry is specifically the configure-scheduling set_* family.
confirmed.event_sequence:
Setup (client A, normal map):
1. A: wl_compositor.create_surface -> S; xdg_wm_base.get_xdg_surface(S) -> XS; xdg_surface.get_toplevel(XS) -> T; (optional) zxdg_decoration set_mode(server_side).
2. A: wl_surface.commit (initial, no buffer) -> compositor sends initial configure; A acks, attaches a wl_shm buffer, commits -> surface MAPS. Server creates View V (V's commit/map listeners fire; xdg_toplevel->base->initialized = true). This is the M3 map path exercised by mapOne().

Open the modal window menu on A's titlebar:
3. USER: move pointer over V's titlebar (Part::Titlebar/Label) and press BTN_RIGHT.
   -> Server::processCursorButton (Server.cc:1315) -> openWindowMenu(V, x, y) (Server.cc:2055): active_menu_ = Menu built by windowmenu::buildFrom, where every actionable row stores m.target = V (the raw View* handle, Windowmenu.cc:18/29). wlr_seat_pointer_notify_clear_focus(seat) makes the menu modal for INPUT only.
   Key fact: input is modal, but the wl_display event loop keeps dispatching client requests. Nothing in the menu-open path stops A's protocol traffic.

A unmaps itself while the menu is up (protocol-legal, role kept alive):
4. A: wl_surface.attach(S, NULL, 0, 0); wl_surface.commit(S).  (A does NOT destroy T/XS.)
   -> server dispatch runs the surface-commit path; wlroots xdg_surface unmap_commit -> reset_xdg_surface sets base->initialized = false (wlr_xdg_surface.c). View::unmap_ listener (View.cc:51-54) fires: sets V.mapped=false, deco->clear() — and NOTHING ELSE. It never notifies Server, never calls closeMenus(). V stays in Server::views; the menu stays open.
   removeView is NOT called (that only runs on xdg_toplevel events.destroy, View.cc:77-79) so viewForHandle(V) still resolves.

User clicks the Maximize row:
5. USER: move pointer over the "Maximize" row and press BTN_LEFT.
   -> Server::handleMenuButton (Server.cc:2277) hit-tests the row, calls activateMenuItem(copy) with copy.action == Act::MaximizeToggle, copy.target == V.
   -> const MenuItem copy = it; closeMenus(); switch: case MaximizeToggle (Server.cc:2257):
        View *v = viewForHandle(copy.target)  -> returns V (alive, just unmapped)
        Output *o = outputForView(v)          -> pure geometry, returns a live Output (Server.cc:751)
        v->setMaximized(!v->isMaximized(), o->workArea())  (View.cc:123)
   -> maximized_ toggles (always a differing value, no mapped/initialized guard), then
        wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_maximized(xdg_toplevel, true)  (View.cc:129)
   -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_set_maximized -> wlr_xdg_surface_schedule_configure -> assert(surface->initialized) with initialized==false -> __assert_fail -> abort. Session dies.

(Contrast: Act::Close on the same corpse calls wlr_xdg_toplevel_send_close — a bare event, no configure — and is safe; the asymmetry is specific to the configure-scheduling set_* family. Iconify/Deiconify hit the same assert via their own set_* paths.)

confirmed.title: focus_before_lock_ survives the referent's destruction and is only pointer-compared: heap-address ABA can focus an arbitrary new window at unlock
confirmed.scenario: Window A focused, session locks (focus_before_lock_=A). Under the lock A's client destroys the toplevel -> removeView frees View A but does NOT clear focus_before_lock_ (unlike workspaces_.clearFocused). A different client then creates a new toplevel and the new View is allocated at A's freed address (same size class - realistic malloc reuse). At unlock, viewForHandle matches the recycled pointer and focusView targets the unrelated new window. No memory unsafety (the match IS a live View), but the unlock focus restore is attacker-influencable/wrong. One-line fix: clear focus_before_lock_ in removeView alongside the other scrubs.
confirmed.event_sequence:
All events are protocol-legal for a real client + a real user at the keyboard/pointer:

1. Client A (xdg_toplevel) connects, maps a window. Server pushes View A into `views` (Server.cc:173-175). onViewMapped -> focusView(A): `focused_view = A`.
   (User optionally clicks it; either way A is the focused_view.)
2. User locks: a session-lock client binds ext_session_lock_manager_v1 and calls lock(). Server blanks heads, sends `locked`. Server::handleSessionLocked runs (Server.cc ~1730-1766): since this is a fresh lock (not a takeover), line 1764 executes `focus_before_lock_ = focused_view;` -> focus_before_lock_ now holds View A's heap address. clearFocus() sets focused_view = nullptr.
3. UNDER THE LOCK, client A destroys its toplevel role (wl_proxy destroy of xdg_toplevel — the ordinary "client closed its window" teardown, or the client simply disconnects). This fires xdg_toplevel events.destroy -> View::toplevel_destroy_ lambda (View.cc:77-79) -> Server::removeView(A) (Server.cc:623). removeView scrubs grabbed_view, pressed_button_view_, autoraise_pending_, icons_, mru_, cycle_ring_, cycle_start_, focused_view, workspaces_.clearFocused, stacking_ — but NOT focus_before_lock_. The `views.erase(it)` at line 648 frees View A's chunk. focus_before_lock_ is now a dangling handle. (removeView's `was_focused` handoff is skipped because focused_view was already parked to nullptr at lock time.)
4. STILL UNDER THE LOCK, a client creates a new xdg_toplevel. new_toplevel handler (Server.cc:173-175) is ungated by the lock: `views.push_back(std::make_unique<View>(...))`. sizeof(View) matches A's freed chunk (same size class) -> the allocator hands back A's address (realistic LIFO free-list reuse after a single same-size free). New View C now lives at focus_before_lock_'s address. focusView is lock-gated (line 895 early-returns while locked), so C is NOT focused and focused_view stays nullptr — C is an unrelated, possibly unmapped/off-workspace window.
5. User unlocks: the lock client calls unlock_and_destroy. locked_ drops, then Server::handleSessionUnlocked (Server.cc:1769) runs: `viewForHandle(focus_before_lock_)` (Server.cc:1783) is a bare `v.get() == handle` scan with no generation/mapped/workspace check — it matches the recycled C. focusView(C) fires, focusing the wrong window instead of the intended topmostViewOnWorkspace fallback. No memory unsafety (C is a live View), but the restored focus is attacker-influencable and wrong.

confirmed.title: deco_destroy_ handler reads its own capture after disconnecting itself (self-destroyed closure, rule violation)
confirmed.scenario: Client creates an xdg_toplevel (View built, attachDecoration later binds deco_destroy_ at View.cc:193), then destroys its zxdg_toplevel_decoration_v1 object while keeping the toplevel (e.g. a GTK app toggling back to CSD). wlroots emits decoration events.destroy -> the lambda runs: deco_request_mode_.disconnect() (fine), then deco_destroy_.disconnect() at View.cc:197 — bt::Listener::disconnect() does `callback = nullptr`, which destroys the std::function target (this very closure) while its operator() is executing — then View.cc:198 `decoration = nullptr;` reads the captured `this` pointer from the destroyed closure's storage. Same shape as the fixed SessionLock crash (calibration bug #2), violating the codified 'self-disconnect must be the last capture-reading statement' rule. Today it is lifetime-UB that happens to read intact bytes (trivially-destructible [this]-only capture in libstdc++ SBO inside the still-alive Listener member), so no observable crash — severity low — but any future capture added to this lambda (e.g. a std::string or the wlr pointer) turns it into a real use-after-free. Fix is a two-line reorder: null `decoration` and disconnect deco_request_mode_ first, self-disconnect last.
confirmed.event_sequence:
1. Client connects; binds wl_compositor, xdg_wm_base, zxdg_decoration_manager_v1 (any GTK/Qt app negotiating decorations).
2. wl_compositor.create_surface -> xdg_wm_base.get_xdg_surface -> xdg_surface.get_toplevel. Server builds the View.
3. zxdg_decoration_manager_v1.get_toplevel_decoration(toplevel); zxdg_toplevel_decoration_v1.set_mode(server_side). Server's new-decoration handler calls View::attachDecoration (View.cc:187), binding deco_request_mode_ and deco_destroy_ (View.cc:189/193).
4. Initial null commit -> xdg_surface.configure -> ack_configure -> wl_surface.attach(buffer) + commit. View maps. (Mapping is not even required — the listener is live from step 3.)
5. Client sends zxdg_toplevel_decoration_v1.destroy while KEEPING the xdg_toplevel (the real-world "GTK app toggles back to CSD" move; protocol-legal — only toplevel-before-decoration is an error per the xdg-decoration spec, encoded as the 'illegal-toplevel-before-deco' order in hostile_client_test.cc:47).
6. Server dispatches: wlroots tears down wlr_xdg_toplevel_decoration_v1 and wl_signal_emit_mutable fires events.destroy -> the deco_destroy_ lambda runs. Line 196 disconnects deco_request_mode_ (fine); line 197 deco_destroy_.disconnect() executes `callback = nullptr` (listener.hpp:33), destroying the std::function target THAT IS CURRENTLY EXECUTING; line 198 `decoration = nullptr;` then reads the captured `this` from the destroyed closure's storage — the out-of-lifetime access. No abort/segfault results today: the [this]-only capture is trivially destructible and lives in libstdc++'s SBO buffer inside the still-alive deco_destroy_ Listener member, so the bytes are intact and ASAN does not flag it. The sequence reaches the UB read on every decoration-only destroy; it cannot be escalated to a crash without code changes (e.g., a future non-trivial capture).

confirmed.title: Windowmenu/iconmenu View handle is identity-by-address: heap reuse redirects Close/Iconify/SendTo/Deiconify to the wrong window
confirmed.scenario: User right-clicks window A's titlebar -> openWindowMenu bakes target = (void*)ViewA into the items (Windowmenu.cc:42, View.hh:26). While the menu is open (removeView, Server.cc:623, never closes it), A's client destroys its toplevel -> View A freed. Another client maps a window -> the new View is a same-size heap allocation, so glibc tcache very likely hands back A's exact address. User now clicks 'Close' (or 'Iconify'/'Send To...') in the still-open menu -> activateMenuItem -> viewForHandle(copy.target) at Server.cc:1783 matches the NEW View by address (Server.cc:2263) -> wlr_xdg_toplevel_send_close fires at an unrelated window. Same hole for iconmenu Deiconify (target set at Server.cc:2153). Not a freed read - viewForHandle only compares against live unique_ptrs - but it is exactly the shape-(b) unscrubbed-cache pattern with the revalidation defeated by ABA. Fix direction: closeMenus() (or scrub matching targets) in removeView when an open menu references the dying View, or make windowID a non-reusable generation id.
confirmed.event_sequence:
Setup: headless server booted, one output. Client A connects, creates wl_surface + xdg_surface + xdg_toplevel (SSD), commits a buffer -> View A mapped at heap address P (fixed-size make_unique<View>).

1. USER: right-click View A's titlebar label. onPointerButton (Server.cc:1218) -> part==Label -> openWindowMenu(A) (Server.cc:1315,2055). The Menu is built via windowmenu::build(A) -> every MenuItem.target = A->windowID() = (void*)P (Windowmenu.cc:18/29/42, View.hh:26). active_menu_ now holds the chain; the modal gate is armed. The menu stores only void* targets and pre-rendered strings — it does NOT deref View A.

2. CLIENT A: destroy the xdg_toplevel (and cascade: decoration/xdg_surface/wl_surface). This is a normal, protocol-legal client teardown. On the next server.dispatch() the View-destroy listener fires -> removeView(A) (Server.cc:623). View A's unique_ptr is erased -> the View at address P is freed. removeView refocuses a survivor but NEVER closes or scrubs active_menu_; the baked target (void*)P is now a dangling identity. The menu stays fully open (modal gate still armed).

3. CLIENT B (any client, incl. a fresh connection): create wl_surface + xdg_surface + xdg_toplevel and commit a buffer. new_toplevel (Server.cc:173) is ungated by active_menu_, so on server.dispatch() a new View is make_unique<View>'d — the same fixed size as A. glibc tcache LIFO hands back the just-freed chunk at address P, so View B lives at P. View B maps.

4. USER: click the 'Close' row (or 'Iconify'/'Send To...'/'Deiconify') in the still-open menu. onPointerButton -> active_menu_ -> handleMenuButton (Server.cc:1222,2274) -> activateMenuItem (Server.cc:2222). copy.target == (void*)P. viewForHandle(P) (Server.cc:1783) scans live views, matches View B (address P), returns B. Server.cc:2263 fires wlr_xdg_toplevel_send_close on View B — an unrelated window the user never targeted. (Iconify/SendTo/Maximize hit B the same way; iconmenu Deiconify target baked at Server.cc:2153 shares the hole.)

No freed memory is read (viewForHandle compares against live unique_ptrs only) — the defect is a wrong-window action via ABA on the unscrubbed baked target. Every step is protocol-legal and user-reachable; the only non-determinism is step 3's exact address reuse, which glibc tcache makes highly likely for a single freed same-size chunk immediately re-allocated.

confirmed.title: PerOutput output_destroy handler frees its own closure (erase_if) then reads captured `this` via maybeSendLocked()
confirmed.scenario: Locker client locks the session (blankOutput creates a heap PerOutput per head; its bt::Listener SBO-stores the [this,p] closure inside the PerOutput). User hot-unplugs a monitor while locked or mid-lock-wait -> wlr_output.events.destroy fires -> handler at SessionLock.cc:86 destroys the blank, then std::erase_if at :88 deletes its OWN PerOutput - freeing the executing closure's storage - then maybeSendLocked() at :91 reads the captured SessionLock* from the freed heap block. Verified empirically: gdb on the build-asan binary during the in-tree 'head destroyed mid-lock-wait' test shows __asan_address_is_poisoned(__closure)==1 at line 91 (region freed by the handler's own erase_if, allocated at blankOutput SessionLock.cc:64); an isolated repro of the identical Listener::thunk->std::function->self-erase pattern aborts with heap-use-after-free. The in-tree test passes only because -O0 codegen keeps the capture in a callee-saved register and ASAN quarantine preserves the bytes - i.e. latent, codegen-dependent UB, not absence of the bug. Exact same shape as the already-fixed SurfaceEntry self-destruction bug (rule: erase-own-Listener must be the LAST capture-reading statement, cf. the correct ordering at SessionLock.cc:163-184). Fix constraint: the post-erase recount is load-bearing (it sends `locked` when the dead head was the last uncommitted one, session_lock_test.cc:379), so keep the recount but route it off the closure, e.g. `SessionLock &self = *this;` stack local taken before the erase, then `self.maybeSendLocked()`.
confirmed.event_sequence: 1. Compositor runs with >=2 heads (e.g. laptop panel + external DP monitor). 2. A lock client (swaylock-shaped) connects: wl_display_connect -> wl_registry bind ext_session_lock_manager_v1. 3. Client sends ext_session_lock_manager_v1.lock. Compositor's onNewLock() calls blankOutput() per head (SessionLock.cc:55-57): each head gets a heap PerOutput whose bt::Listener output_destroy SBO-stores the [this, p] closure inside that same PerOutput allocation. 4. Before every head has committed a post-blank frame (mid-lock-wait; a frame or two of margin, ~16-32ms - or at ANY later time while locked, since per_output_ entries persist until unlock), the user hot-unplugs the external monitor. 5. The DRM backend fires wlr_output.events.destroy -> wl_signal_emit_mutable invokes the PerOutput::output_destroy handler (SessionLock.cc:86): it destroys the blank rect (:87), then std::erase_if(per_output_) (:88) deletes its OWN PerOutput - running ~bt::Listener (which assigns nullptr into the std::function currently mid-invocation) and freeing the closure's storage - then maybeSendLocked() (:91) reads the captured SessionLock* from the freed heap block. On the -O0/ASAN-quarantine build this read is latent (capture happens to sit in a callee-saved register); on an optimized or differently-compiled build the load goes through the freed block -> garbage SessionLock* -> wild reads in maybeSendLocked's per_output_ loop -> segfault of the live dogfooded session. No hostile client is needed: the client is a perfectly well-behaved locker and the trigger is a physical unplug. NOTE: this exact sequence is already produced by the in-tree test "head destroyed mid-lock-wait" (tests/system/session_lock_test.cc:379-419) via destroyOutputForTest(1) - the UB executes on every test run today and passes only by codegen accident.

confirmed.title: Ignored async-send failures in SniMenu wedge sni_menu_ forever, permanently disabling every compositor menu
confirmed.scenario: The session dbus-daemon dies or restarts. Case A (race): before the Host's fd source dispatches the disconnect, the user right-clicks a menu-only tray icon in the slit; openSniContextMenu (Server.cc:2115) passes the sni_host_->ok() check (Host hasn't noticed yet), constructs SniMenu, and open()'s sd_bus_call_method_async/sd_bus_match_signal_async return -ENOTCONN - both return values ignored (SniMenu.cc:41-50), so no slot, no reply, no method-call timeout will ever fire. Case B (no race needed): the daemon dies while an AboutToShow/GetLayout is legitimately in flight; sd-bus dispatches the pending reply with a synthetic Disconnected error, onAboutToShow calls fetchLayout, whose sd_bus_call_method_async on the now-closing bus fails and is ignored (SniMenu.cc:66-72) - on_layout_ is never invoked, so neither showDbusMenu nor the deferred fallback/reset runs. Either way Server::sni_menu_ stays non-null for the rest of the session, and every menu opener - openRootMenu (Server.cc:2011), openWindowMenu (2056), openToolbarMenu (2066), openSlitMenu (2075), openSniContextMenu (2125), openIconMenu (2160) - returns early. closeMenus (the only reset) is unreachable by normal input: handleMenuButton/handleMenuKey require active_menu_, which is null. Recovery only via session lock (handleSessionLocked gates on active_menu_ too, so not even that - Server.cc:1744) or a reconfigure/style reload (Server.cc:428). No freed read - a functional lockup of all menus, in the same client-controlled-timing family.
confirmed.event_sequence:
1. Session running; compositor's sni::Host owns org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher on the session bus. A real tray app (electron/udiskie-style) registers a StatusNotifierItem advertising Menu=/MenuBar and serves com.canonical.dbusmenu there; its icon materializes in the slit.
2. User right-clicks the icon: BTN_RIGHT press over the slit item -> Server::processCursorButton slit hit-test (Server.cc:1275-1285) -> openSniContextMenu (2115). Gate at 2121/2125 passes; sni_menu_ is constructed and SniMenu::open() flushes AboutToShow to the app. active_menu_ stays null across the async round-trip.
3. While the AboutToShow reply is in flight (tens of ms with a real app; longer if the app is slow), the session dbus-daemon dies - SIGKILL, OOM-kill, crash, or `systemctl --user restart dbus` (equivalently, Case A: the daemon dies just before the click, in the window before the Host's fd source next dispatches - ok() is still true so the opener gate passes and both async sends in open() fail with -ENOTCONN, return values ignored at SniMenu.cc:41-50).
4. Next compositor event-loop iteration: the Host's fd source fires (HUP). Host::drain (SniHost.cc:336-347) pumps sd_bus_process; the CLOSING bus dispatches a synthetic "Connection terminated" error reply into SniMenu::onAboutToShow (SniMenu.cc:58-63), which ignores the error and calls fetchLayout(); its sd_bus_call_method_async on the closing bus returns -ENOTCONN, ignored (SniMenu.cc:67-72) - no layout_slot_ installed. The following sd_bus_process returns <0 and drain calls teardownBus(): fd+timer sources removed, bus freed. Host never notifies Server; sni_menu_ is not touched.
5. Terminal wedged state: sni_menu_ != nullptr and active_menu_ == nullptr forever. on_layout_ never ran, so neither showDbusMenu (Server.cc:2141) nor the scheduleSniMenuReset fallback (2138) ever executes, and with the bus gone no reply, signal, or 25s method timeout can ever pump it.
6. User-visible lockup for the rest of the session: right-click desktop -> openRootMenu returns at Server.cc:2011; Alt+Space/titlebar -> openWindowMenu returns at 2056; toolbar menu 2066, slit menu 2075, any tray icon 2125, icon menu 2160 - all silently refuse. Escape/clicks cannot recover: handleMenuButton (1222) and handleMenuKey (1928, 2294) are gated on active_menu_, which is null; handleSessionLocked's closeMenus is gated the same way (1744). Only restyle()/reconfigure (428) or session end (~Server, 601-605) resets sni_menu_. Not a freed read - a permanent functional lockup of all compositor menus at client-controlled (daemon-death) timing.

confirmed.title: Host::teardownBus leaves items_ populated and fires no itemRemoved - slit renders dead D-Bus items after a bus death
confirmed.scenario: The session bus daemon dies; the Host's fd source fires, sd_bus_process returns <0, drain() calls teardownBus (SniHost.cc:340-343), which clears regs_ and closes the bus but does NOT clear items_ and fires no events. Slit::refresh is never triggered, so item_count_ and the rendered cells stay stale: the tray keeps showing icons for connections that no longer exist until some unrelated refresh (style change, item event on a bus that will never speak again). No memory unsafety - the click path at Server.cc:1280 checks host->ok() (now false) so left/middle clicks on the dead cells are swallowed and right-click falls through to openSlitMenu - but the compositor UI references dead D-Bus objects indefinitely, and any future click-path change that drops the ok() check inherits a stale-index read into a vector that no event will ever fix. Fix shape: teardownBus should drain items_ through the itemRemoved event (or at least clear items_ and fire one refresh).
confirmed.event_sequence:
1. Compositor boots with a live session bus; sni::Host claims org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher, Server::installSniHostEvents wires HostEvents to Slit::refresh (src/Server.cc:720-730).
2. A real SNI app (nm-applet, blueman, or the test's SniMockChild) calls RegisterStatusNotifierItem; the Host's GetAll materializes an sni::Item; itemAdded fires -> Slit::refresh renders one icon cell and applies a strut (src/Slit.cc:120-157).
3. The session bus daemon itself dies (crash or `kill -9` of dbus-daemon/dbus-broker for the session — an ordinary systemd-user or OOM casualty; no Wayland protocol involvement, all Wayland traffic stays legal and idle).
4. The compositor's wl_event_loop wakes the Host's fd source with HUP/READABLE (Cb::onFd, src/SniHost.cc:93-96) -> drain() -> sd_bus_process dispatches the synthesized org.freedesktop.DBus.Local Disconnected message, next pass returns <0 -> teardownBus() (src/SniHost.cc:328-334) clears regs_, removes fd/timer sources, closes bus_ (ok() now false). items_ is NOT cleared, no itemRemoved/refresh fires — dropRegistration (SniHost.cc:473, the only itemRemoved emitter) is not on this path.
5. Steady state (the bug): the slit keeps rendering the dead icon, the ghost strut keeps shrinking the work area, and item_count_ stays 1 forever (the only host-driven refresh is the HostEvents fan-out, which will never fire again).
6. User input on the stale cell: pointer moves over the icon, left/middle press hits Server.cc:1280-1284 — idx>=0 but host->ok() is false, so the click is swallowed with no effect; right-click falls to openSlitMenu (Server.cc:1286-88); every press over the slit rectangle is swallowed as chrome (Server.cc:1289) — a permanent input dead-zone.
IMPORTANT HONESTY NOTE: the terminal observable is stale rendering + ghost strut + click dead-zone. There is NO freed read and NO abort at the endpoint — the ok() gate at Server.cc:1284 and the idx < items().size() bounds check keep the stale items_ read memory-safe (sni::Item is value-typed, Sni.hh:37, no bus pointers). The finding is reachable exactly as claimed; its severity ceiling is stale-UI, not UAF.

confirmed.title: In-flight paste Writer (heap + pipe fd + wl_event_source) leaks at compositor shutdown
confirmed.scenario: User takes a region screenshot (clipboard now holds a ClipboardImage); a client calls wl_data_offer.receive and then stops reading its pipe end (pipe buffer fills, the Writer parks on WL_EVENT_WRITABLE); user quits the compositor. ~Server (src/Server.cc:578-621) removes sni_menu_reset_idle_ and the TimerRegistry's sources but has no registry of live paste Writers, and wl_display_destroy's wl_event_loop_destroy does not free remaining event sources or their user data. The Writer struct, its blob shared_ptr ref, the fd, and the wl_event_source all leak at exit. NOT a use-after-free: no event-loop dispatch runs after teardown begins, so writerCb can never fire against freed state — this only shows up under LSAN/valgrind on shutdown-with-slow-paster tests. Everything else in the subsystem checked out clean: impl->destroy ownership, writer-vs-replacement (tested at tests/system/clipboard_image_test.cc:58), overlay teardown mid-drag (global-scene parentage + null-guarded destroy from cancel/finish/~Server), output death mid-drag (null-safe activeSceneOutput -> captureRegion bails), and the seat listener-list asserts (disconnected at Server.cc:598-599).
confirmed.event_sequence:
1. USER: presses Super+F7 (region-screenshot bind), moves pointer to (x0,y0), presses BTN_LEFT, drags to (x0+W,y0+H), releases. Server.cc:1096-1103: captureRegion -> screenshot::encodePng -> ClipboardImage::create(display, blob) -> wlr_seat_set_selection(seat, &ci->base, ...). The focused client's wl_data_device gets a wl_data_offer advertising "image/png".
2. CLIENT (any clipboard manager / wl-paste): pipe(fds); wl_data_offer.receive("image/png", fds[1]); close(fds[1]) locally; wl_display_flush. Compositor dispatch: wlroots data-offer receive handler -> wlr_data_source impl->send == ciSend (ClipboardImage.cc:41-50): sets O_NONBLOCK on the dup'd fd, news Writer{blob ref, 0, fd}, wl_event_loop_add_fd(display loop, WL_EVENT_WRITABLE, writerCb, w).
3. CLIENT: never reads fds[0] (stalled/suspended paster). Compositor loop dispatches writerCb; write() fills the pipe (64 KiB default) then returns EAGAIN; writerCb returns 0 (ClipboardImage.cc:33) and the source stays parked on WL_EVENT_WRITABLE with the Writer mid-blob. (Requires PNG > pipe capacity — any real screen region qualifies; for a tiny PNG the same parked state exists in the window between receive and the next loop iteration, i.e. if the quit is processed in the same dispatch batch.)
4. USER: quits the compositor (exit keybinding / SIGTERM ends the run loop). ~Server (Server.cc:578-621) removes sni_menu_reset_idle_ and the TimerRegistry/SniHost sources — no code path knows about the Writer (anonymous-namespace type, no registry; ciDestroy deliberately leaves in-flight writers alone). wl_display_destroy_clients tears down the client connection WITHOUT dispatching the loop (a closed read end only makes the fd HUP-ready; writerCb never runs again). wl_display_destroy -> wl_event_loop_destroy frees the loop but, per libwayland's documented contract, does NOT free still-registered fd sources or their user data. RESULT: the Writer struct, its ClipboardImage::Blob shared_ptr ref (pinning the whole PNG vector), the dup'd pipe write fd, and the wl_event_source all leak at exit. No freed read and no abort occur — nothing dispatches after teardown begins — this is a pure shutdown leak, LSAN/valgrind-visible only.

confirmed.title: Runtime libseat session death aborts: session_active listener never disconnected before wlr_session_destroy's empty-list assert
confirmed.scenario: User runs the compositor live on DRM/TTY (the dogfood configuration, so session_ is non-null and session_active is connected). seatd crashes or systemd-logind is restarted (or any libseat fd HANGUP/ERROR, or a libseat_dispatch failure) -> wlroots libseat_event calls wlr_session_destroy at runtime (wlroots-0.20.1 backend/session/session.c:45,50). That emits session->events.destroy (Server listens to it nowhere; only the DRM child backend does, tearing down all outputs - which the onOutputDestroyed live path survives), then executes assert(wl_list_empty(&session->events.active.listener_list)) at session.c:316. Server::session_active (connected Server.cc:126, disconnected only in ~Server at Server.cc:584, which never ran) is still chained -> SIGABRT kills the live session. If wlroots were built with asserts off, the session struct is freed with our wl_listener still linked into it, and ~Server's session_active.disconnect() later performs wl_list_remove on freed heap (corruption). Fix shape: connect a listener to session_->events.destroy that disconnects session_active and nulls session_.
confirmed.event_sequence:
No Wayland-protocol events are needed at all — the trigger is an out-of-band libseat event, which makes it strictly easier to reach than any hostile-client shape. Exact live sequence in the dogfood configuration:

1. User logs into a bare VT (e.g. tty2) and runs blackboxai. `wlr_backend_autocreate(loop, &session_)` (src/Server.cc:112) opens a libseat session via systemd-logind (or seatd), so `session_` is non-null and `session_active.connect(&session_->events.active, ...)` runs (src/Server.cc:125-130). The compositor is now the user's live session; any number of ordinary clients may be running (they play no role).
2. From ssh or another VT — or simply as a side effect of a distro package upgrade — the libseat controller dies: `sudo systemctl restart systemd-logind` (logind seat) or `sudo pkill -9 seatd` (seatd). The controller side of the libseat socket closes.
3. The compositor's wl_event_loop wakes on the libseat fd with EPOLLHUP/EPOLLERR. wlroots backend/session/session.c `libseat_event()` calls `wlr_session_destroy(session)` at runtime (session.c:45; the same happens on a `libseat_dispatch` failure at :50).
4. `wlr_session_destroy` emits `session->events.destroy` (session.c:314). Server listens nowhere on that signal; only the DRM/libinput child backends react, removing their own listeners and destroying their outputs (Server::onOutputDestroyed handles live output death, so nothing crashes here).
5. session.c:316: `assert(wl_list_empty(&session->events.active.listener_list))`. Server's `session_active` wl_listener is still chained (its only disconnect is `~Server`, src/Server.cc:584, which has not run) -> assert fails -> SIGABRT, killing the user's live session. Verified compiled-in: `strings /usr/lib64/libwlroots-0.20.so` contains the literal `wl_list_empty(&session->events.active.listener_list)` (wlroots-0.20.1-1.fc44).
6. (NDEBUG-wlroots variant) the assert is absent, `free(session)` runs at session.c:332 with our listener still linked; later `~Server`'s `session_active.disconnect()` executes `wl_list_remove` against the freed session struct — a heap UAF write.

Note on harness reachability: the existing headless test harness cannot reach this path unmodified — under `Server(/*headless=*/true)` the backend is `wlr_headless_backend_create` and `session_` stays null (src/Server.hh:396), so the listener is never connected; `wlr_session_create` in a test would require a running seatd, which CI does not have. The production sequence above is fully user-producible, hence reachable=true; the doctest needs a one-line test seam (below).
